ShmError.doc: Single failure channel for shm operations. Targets map to idiomatic error types.

ShmLockKind.doc: Names the eight logical locks the shm protocol uses. WRITE excludes other writers. CHECKPOINT excludes other checkpointers. RECOVER excludes other recoverers. READ_K(0..4) excludes writers of read_marks[k]. The mapping to OS primitives lives in target mapping.md files.

ShmLockMode.doc: Lock acquisition mode. Shared = many readers; Exclusive = sole holder.

ShmHeaderRecord.doc: 48-byte wal-index header record. Stored TWICE back-to-back at offset 0 of region 0; readers accept only when both copies are byte-identical AND the Fibonacci checksum over the first 40 bytes validates. is_init becomes 1 once a writer has populated the record. big_endian_checksums mirrors the WAL magic choice. salts mirror the WAL header's current salts; rolling them in the WAL must be followed by re-initializing this record.

ShmCheckpointInfo.doc: Bytes 96..136 of region 0. n_backfill is the number of WAL frames already copied to the main DB file. read_marks[5] are the five read-mark slots; index 0 is permanently 0. n_backfill_attempted is the optimistic intent counter used by checkpointers.

ShmHashRegion.doc: One 32 KiB hash region. a_pgno[k] holds the page_number of the frame whose region-relative index is k. a_hash[h] holds (region-index + 1) into a_pgno, with 0 meaning empty. Lookup: probe a_hash via hash(p) = (p * 383) mod NSLOT with linear probe; resolve to a_pgno; the frame number is region_base + a_pgno_index + 1. Region 0 has NPAGE_ONE entries (4062); regions 1..N have NPAGE entries (4096).

ShmState.doc: Per-process handle for an open shm file. db_path is the database path (the shm path is derived as db_path + '-shm'). header is the validated current header (most recently read copy, after both-copies-agree check). regions is the set of currently-mapped 32 KiB hash regions, indexed by region_index. mark_held names the READ(k) slot this process holds, if any (for Reader role); 0xFFFFFFFF means none.

ReaderHandle.doc: Returned by shm_reader_open. mark_index is the READ(k) slot the reader has SHARED-locked. mx_frame is the WAL frame number this reader's snapshot is pinned to. mark_index = 0 means the special 'no WAL' snapshot (mx_frame = 0).

WriterHandle.doc: Returned by shm_writer_begin. Holds EXCLUSIVE on WRITE for its lifetime; released by shm_writer_commit or shm_writer_rollback. start_mx_frame snapshots the mx_frame at begin so commit can compute frames_written.

CheckpointHandle.doc: Returned by shm_checkpoint_begin. Holds EXCLUSIVE on CHECKPOINT for its lifetime; released by shm_checkpoint_end. barrier_frame is the highest frame the checkpointer is allowed to backfill past, computed from active read marks at begin time.

ShmLookupResult.doc: Result of a page lookup in the shm hash table. Found gives the frame_number of the LATEST frame for that page within [1, mx_frame]. NotFound means the page is not in the WAL (caller falls back to main DB file).

shm_open.doc: Open or create the shm file at `{db_path}-shm`. If the file is shorter than SHM_REGION_SIZE OR the two header copies disagree OR the header checksum fails OR the version field doesn't match SHM_VERSION, run shm_recover internally to reconstruct from WAL frames. Returns a ShmState with the validated header and at least region 0 mapped. Does NOT acquire any of the named locks; caller does that explicitly via reader/writer/checkpoint flows.

shm_recover.doc: Reconstruct shm contents from the on-disk WAL. Acquires EXCLUSIVE on RECOVER; if another process completed recovery while we waited, releases and returns the now-valid state. Otherwise: truncates shm to one region, scans WAL frames forward applying base wal protocol, populates the hash table for frames 1..mx_frame, writes both header copies with a barrier between, releases RECOVER. Idempotent. Read-only against the WAL.

shm_lock_acquire.doc: Acquire one of the named locks in the requested mode. Blocks (or returns err with a 'busy' message — target choice) if the lock is incompatibly held. Mapping to OS primitives is target-specific.

shm_lock_try_acquire.doc: Non-blocking lock acquisition. Returns Some(()) on success, None if the lock is incompatibly held by another process. Used by readers when probing READ(k) slots.

shm_lock_release.doc: Release a previously acquired lock. Idempotent if not held.

shm_reader_open.doc: Open a reader snapshot. Probes read_marks[1..4] for a slot already pinned to current mx_frame; if found, takes SHARED on that READ(k) and returns. Otherwise tries to acquire EXCLUSIVE on a free READ(k), writes mx_frame into read_marks[k], downgrades to SHARED. If all 1..4 marks are busy, falls back to SHARED on READ(0) (mx_frame = 0, 'no WAL' snapshot). Returns ReaderHandle.

shm_reader_close.doc: Release the SHARED lock on READ(handle.mark_index). Leaves read_marks[k] populated as a hint for future readers. Idempotent.

shm_lookup_page.doc: Look up a page in the shm hash table for the reader's snapshot. Probes the appropriate region(s) within [1, handle.mx_frame], using hash(p) = (p * 383) mod NSLOT with linear probe. Returns Found(frame_number) for the LATEST matching frame, NotFound if absent. Reads only — does not mutate shm state.

shm_writer_begin.doc: Acquire EXCLUSIVE on WRITE. Re-reads the header to refresh local view in case another writer committed between this writer's last touch and now. Returns WriterHandle with start_mx_frame = current header.mx_frame.

shm_writer_append.doc: Add a (page_number, frame_no) entry to the shm hash table. If frame_no's region is not yet mapped, extends the shm file by SHM_REGION_SIZE and maps the new region. Inserts via linear probe; if an existing entry for page_number is found in this region, overwrites it (latest-wins inside region). Increments handle.frames_pending_count.

shm_writer_commit.doc: Publish the writer's changes by updating the header. Pre-condition: the WAL frames covered by handle's appends have already been fsynced per the connection's SyncLevel (pin SHM13). Writes header copy 1 (mx_frame, n_page, frame_checksum, salts, change_counter+1), issues a memory barrier, writes header copy 2 (identical bytes), issues a memory barrier, releases EXCLUSIVE on WRITE.

shm_writer_rollback.doc: Abandon the writer session without publishing. The shm hash table may have been mutated by shm_writer_append calls; those mutations are stale (point to WAL frames that won't exist). Recovery on next access (or another writer overwriting) will correct them. Releases EXCLUSIVE on WRITE.

shm_checkpoint_begin.doc: Acquire EXCLUSIVE on CHECKPOINT. Computes barrier_frame: starts at header.mx_frame; for each k in 1..4, if some process holds SHARED on READ(k) AND read_marks[k] != 0, lowers barrier_frame to min(barrier_frame, read_marks[k]). Returns CheckpointHandle.

shm_checkpoint_advance.doc: Update n_backfill in the checkpoint info block to advanced_frame (must be <= handle.barrier_frame). Caller has already copied the relevant frames into the main DB file. If advanced_frame == header.mx_frame AND no readers hold READ(1..4), the caller may follow with a salt-roll reset (delegated to the base wal_checkpoint).

shm_hash.doc: The shm hash function: (page_number * 383) mod SHM_HASHTABLE_NSLOT. Pure; targets MAY inline. Exposed in the shape surface for cross-target equivalence tests.

shm_header_checksum.doc: Compute the (c0, c1) Fibonacci-style checksum over the first 40 bytes of an encoded ShmHeaderRecord. Initial state (0, 0); same checksum step as wal_checksum_step. Used both when writing the header (to populate checksum_c0/c1) and when reading (to validate).

shm_encode_header_record.doc: Encode a ShmHeaderRecord into 48 host-endian bytes. checksum_c0/c1 in the input MUST already be valid (computed by shm_header_checksum over the first 40 bytes); this function does not recompute. Used for both header copies on commit.

shm_decode_header_record.doc: Decode 48 bytes into a ShmHeaderRecord. Returns err(ShmError) on checksum mismatch or version mismatch. Caller is responsible for comparing two decoded copies for byte-identity before accepting.
